evidence.claim: Kishida was Japan's prime minister in 2022, a House of Representatives member, and the Hiroshima 1st District representative; the profile also records his prior foreign and defense posts.
evidence.title: KISHIDA Fumio (The Cabinet)
evidence.excerpt: Kishida was Japan's prime minister in 2022, a House of Representatives member, and the Hiroshima 1st District representative; the profile also records his prior foreign and defense posts.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Primary government biography maintained by the PMO; direct office and role evidence.
evidence.period_fit: Directly establishes ruler office and political identity during 2022.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Directly Kishida's official profile; not inferred.

evidence.claim: Kishida condemned Abe's shooting as an unforgivable and despicable act during an election campaign and said the government would take every possible measure.
evidence.title: Press Conference by the Prime Minister on the Attack Perpetrated against Former Prime Minister ABE Shinzo
evidence.excerpt: Kishida condemned Abe's shooting as an unforgivable and despicable act during an election campaign and said the government would take every possible measure.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Direct PMO transcript from the day of the attack.
evidence.period_fit: Immediate response to a major domestic political killing in 2022.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Direct first-person response by Kishida as prime minister.
contrary_evidence: The attack exposed a serious VIP-security failure that Kishida inherited rather than caused.

evidence.claim: The National Police Agency said it could not protect Abe's life, created a verification and review team, and produced a report on August 25, 2022 to improve VIP protection.
evidence.title: トピックスI　要人警護の強化に係る警察の取組
evidence.excerpt: The National Police Agency said it could not protect Abe's life, created a verification and review team, and produced a report on August 25, 2022 to improve VIP protection.
evidence.source_locator: opening paragraphs on the Abe shooting and the August 25 report
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Primary police-white-paper material describing the institution's own review of the 2022 failure.
evidence.period_fit: Retrospective official account of 2022 domestic-security failure and remedy.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Institutional response under Kishida's cabinet, not a private act by Kishida alone.
contrary_evidence: This is remedial action after failure, not proof of prior effective protection.

evidence.claim: The National Police Agency chief said he would resign to take responsibility for Abe's murder and described the need for a fresh start and a new security plan.
evidence.title: Japan police chief to resign over Abe shooting, citing 'fresh start'
evidence.excerpt: The National Police Agency chief said he would resign to take responsibility for Abe's murder and described the need for a fresh start and a new security plan.
evidence.source_locator: lead paragraphs and quoted resignation explanation
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Reuters is strong independent monitoring; this is a republished wire report.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Indirect but explicit to the Kishida-led police apparatus.
contrary_evidence: The report reflects failure and correction rather than effective prevention.

evidence.claim: Kishida said the new chair of the National Public Safety Commission must thoroughly verify the killing of former Prime Minister Abe and rebuild security arrangements.
evidence.title: Press Conference by Prime Minster Kishida
evidence.excerpt: Kishida said the new chair of the National Public Safety Commission must thoroughly verify the killing of former Prime Minister Abe and rebuild security arrangements.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Direct PMO transcript of Kishida's cabinet-reshuffle instructions.
evidence.period_fit: Direct 2022 institutional response to the assassination shock.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Direct first-person instruction by Kishida as prime minister.
contrary_evidence: It follows a major failure rather than demonstrating a preexisting protective record.

evidence.claim: Kishida instructed that religious groups must obey laws and ordinances and that the government should strengthen consultation and victim-support measures for wrongful business practices and related harm.
evidence.title: Press Conference by Prime Minster Kishida
evidence.excerpt: Kishida instructed that religious groups must obey laws and ordinances and that the government should strengthen consultation and victim-support measures for wrongful business practices and related harm.
evidence.source_locator: instructions on two points in the opening statement
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Direct PMO transcript with explicit instructions to his cabinet and ministries.
evidence.period_fit: Direct 2022 response to the Unification Church crisis.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Direct first-person instruction by Kishida as prime minister.
contrary_evidence: The statement is remedial and does not erase the underlying scandal.

evidence.claim: Kishida accepted criticism that his explanation for the state funeral was insufficient while the funeral drew widespread public opposition.
evidence.title: Japan PM defends decision on state funeral for Abe
evidence.excerpt: Kishida accepted criticism that his explanation for the state funeral was insufficient while the funeral drew widespread public opposition.
evidence.source_locator: report body and quoted parliamentary response
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Reuters wire report republished by Euronews; useful for contemporaneous reaction and protest climate.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Directly attributed to Kishida's handling of the funeral decision.
contrary_evidence: Public backlash is evidence of controversy, not of state repression by Kishida.

evidence.claim: Reuters reported that police officers were on patrol while protesters and local residents expressed opposition around Abe's state funeral, which had become a flashpoint for public anger.
evidence.title: Japan prepares for slain PM Shinzo Abe's state funeral
evidence.excerpt: Reuters reported that police officers were on patrol while protesters and local residents expressed opposition around Abe's state funeral, which had become a flashpoint for public anger.
evidence.source_locator: story text summary of preparations and public reaction
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Reuters text summary of contemporaneous reporting; direct but republished in archive form.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Attributed to the Kishida government decision to hold the funeral.
contrary_evidence: The report shows protest tolerated and policed, not crushed.

evidence.claim: Kishida said he was listening steadfastly to public voices on relationships with the former Unification Church and would set up consultation services and legal support to provide relief and prevent recurrence.
evidence.title: Policy Speech by Prime Minister KISHIDA Fumio to the 210th Session of the Diet
evidence.excerpt: Kishida said he was listening steadfastly to public voices on relationships with the former Unification Church and would set up consultation services and legal support to provide relief and prevent recurrence.
evidence.source_locator: speech section on the former Unification Church and relief measures
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Direct PMO transcript of a major Diet policy speech.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Direct first-person policy commitment by Kishida as prime minister.
contrary_evidence: This is a remedial response after the crisis, not evidence of prior prevention.

evidence.claim: Kishida ordered an investigation into the Unification Church after Abe's assassination revealed close ties between the church and ruling party lawmakers.
evidence.title: Japan PM orders probe into Unification Church links to ruling party members
evidence.excerpt: Kishida ordered an investigation into the Unification Church after Abe's assassination revealed close ties between the church and ruling party lawmakers.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Reuters is strong independent monitoring; this is a republished wire report.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Directly attributed to Kishida's order as prime minister.
contrary_evidence: The probe is accountability after harm, not a preventive safety success in itself.

evidence.claim: The Japanese government launched a probe into the Unification Church that could strip the group of legal status and tax exemptions.
evidence.title: Japan govt begins Unification Church probe amid anger over ties with ruling party
evidence.excerpt: The Japanese government launched a probe into the Unification Church that could strip the group of legal status and tax exemptions.
evidence.source_locator: lead paragraph and subsequent explanation of the probe
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Reuters is strong independent monitoring; this is a republished wire report.
contrary_evidence: This remains an investigative and legal step, not proof of improved protection yet.

evidence.claim: Kishida said he met directly with people harmed by the former Unification Church, ordered a new law within constitutional limits, and set up a government-wide support system with the Japan Legal Support Center and other bodies.
evidence.title: Press Conference by Prime Minister Kishida
evidence.excerpt: Kishida said he met directly with people harmed by the former Unification Church, ordered a new law within constitutional limits, and set up a government-wide support system with the Japan Legal Support Center and other bodies.
evidence.source_locator: opening statement on the relief law and follow-up support
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Direct PMO transcript with explicit account of legislative and administrative action.
evidence.period_fit: Direct end-of-year 2022 remedy and accountability action.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Direct first-person leadership claim by Kishida as prime minister.
contrary_evidence: Relief legislation mitigates harm but does not undo the harm already done.

unresolved_gaps: Direct cabinet-level records on Kishida's private command-and-control choices around safeguards, emergency procedures, and technical nuclear governance are thin.
Direct evidence of behind-the-scenes mediation, ceasefire brokerage, or proxy-control choices is thin.
The dossier remains thin on a ruler-specific pre-July 2022 domestic protection record, so most of the strong evidence is reactive to the Abe assassination and the Unification Church fallout.
Direct evidence of court, media, or election-administration capture attempts by Kishida is thin; most negative evidence is baseline openness plus remedial scandal cleanup.
Direct anti-capture, procurement, or favoritism evidence is thin relative to the amount of policy and macroeconomic material.
Subgroup-specific uptake and outcome evidence for poverty, disability, migrants, and regional disparities remains thin.
The dossier lacks direct 2022 evidence on Kishida's own assets, gifts, campaign finance, hidden conflicts, or family enrichment.
Independent evaluation of New Capitalism implementation and the causal contribution of Kishida's team remains limited; several follow-up items are government self-assessments or macro context.
